## 1. The home: a new `.claude/rules/authoring.md`

Create it with exactly this content (it is the page INC-1 landed and its reviewer accepted word for word against criteria 1, 2 and 3; recover it verbatim with `git show origin/claude/authoring-rule-form-matching-c5ygkt--INC-1:.claude/rules/authoring.md`):

```
---
paths:
  - "skills/**"
  - "agents/**"
---
# The form of a rule

A rule fails in a particular way, and the form that repairs it follows from
that way and not from taste. The rows below come from measured head-to-head
wording tests (obra/superpowers, `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md`, "Match the
Form to the Failure"), so a row changes when a new measurement says so.

Find the failure your rule prevents, then write it in the form that column
names.

| Failure class | Form that works | Form that fails | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A rule skipped under pressure | A prohibition that carries its price and quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation it counters | An unpriced reminder to keep the rule in mind | Under pressure an agent trades away a rule whose cost of skipping is unnamed, and an unquoted excuse stays available. |
| A wrong output shape | A recipe that states what the output is | A list of prohibitions | A ban names what not to emit and leaves the shape unstated, which measured worse than no guidance at all. |
| An omitted required element | A required slot in the schema or the template | Prose in the body asking for the element | A slot makes the omission visible in the artefact, while prose is satisfied by an agent that believes it complied. |
| Behaviour that depends on a condition | A rule keyed to an observable predicate | A judgement call, or an exemption bolted onto the general rule | A predicate the agent can evaluate decides both branches, and a judgement call decides neither. |

Never patch a working rule with an exemption clause. Re-cut the rule on an
observable predicate instead, and state each branch on its own: one appended
exemption measured a working rule down from consistent to noisy.

This page stays in this checkout rather than in the shipped brief because it
binds whoever writes a page here, not an agent at run time.
```

Plain bash, no framework: each case is a shell condition calling `ok "<what holds>"` or `no "<what does not>"`, both defined at the top of the file, with `$root` as the repository root. Sections open with `echo` then `echo "=== <section title>"`. Where a condition needs more than grep, the file's own style is either an inline `node -e '...' If conventions need writing down, extend the header comment at the top of `test-repo.sh`; nothing in this plan requires it.

## The table parser the row cases share

Four of the cases need the table split into cells. Write one helper script — the `mktemp -d` plus quoted heredoc pattern above — taking `root`, a failure-class regex source and a JSON array of marker regex sources on argv, and run it once per row. It: reads `$root/.claude/rules/authoring.md`; takes every line whose trimmed form starts with `|`; treats the first as the header and drops any line that is only pipes, dashes, colons and spaces; splits a row on `|`, drops the empty first and last fields, trims each cell; selects the body rows whose cell 1 matches the failure-class regex, case-insensitively, and exits non-zero unless exactly one matches; then asserts every marker matches cell 2 and no marker matches cell 3, exiting non-zero with a message naming the marker and the cell that broke it. Matching is case-insensitive throughout.

## The cases

Criterion 1 — a table of exactly four rows, four named parts each.

1. Shape. Parse the table: exactly four body rows; each splits into exactly four cells; no cell is empty. Break: add a fifth row, delete one, or blank any cell — in particular the `form that fails` cell of any row.
2. Column order. The header row's cells match, in order: `failure` in cell 1, `works` in cell 2, `fails` in cell 3, `why` or `reason` in cell 4. Break: swap the `Form that works` and `Form that fails` headers — which inverts all four rows at once while every cell keeps its text, and is why this case is separate from case 1.
3. One-sentence reason. Every body row's fourth cell contains exactly one full stop, at its end (regex: one or more non-full-stop characters, then a full stop, anchored both ends). Break: split any reason cell into two sentences, or empty it.

Criterion 2 and criterion 5 — the four rows, each guarded against its own inversion. One case per row, each run of the shared parser above, each asserting the markers are all in the winning cell and none of them in the failing cell.

4. Row 1. Failure-class regex `skipped under pressure`. Markers: `prohibition`; `price` with word boundaries on both sides, so the failing form's `unpriced` cannot satisfy it; `verbatim`; `rationalisation`. Breaks, each independently red: swap cells 2 and 3 of the row (the failing form names no prohibition); replace `A prohibition` in cell 2 with `A reminder`; delete `carries its price and ` from cell 2 (criterion 6, the price); delete `, verbatim,` from cell 2 or replace `quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation it counters` with `names the rationalisation it counters` (criterion 6, the verbatim rationalisation); move any marker's wording into cell 3.
5. Row 2. Failure-class regex `output shape`. Markers: `recipe`; `output`. Breaks: swap cells 2 and 3, so the wrong output shape is paired with a list of prohibitions — the form measured to lose against it (criterion 5); replace cell 2 with `A list of prohibitions`; drop `what the output is` from cell 2.
6. Row 3. Failure-class regex `omitted required element`. Markers: `slot` with word boundaries; `schema` or `template`. Breaks: swap cells 2 and 3, so the omission is paired with prose in the body (criterion 5); replace cell 2 with `Prose in the body asking for the element`; drop `in the schema or the template` from cell 2.
7. Row 4. Failure-class regex `depends on a condition`. Marker: `observable predicate`. Breaks: swap cells 2 and 3, so the conditional behaviour is paired with a judgement call or a bolted-on exemption (criterion 5); replace `keyed to an observable predicate` in cell 2 with `left to the agent's judgement`.

Criterion 3 and criterion 6 — the exemption-clause ban.

8. The ban. Split the page on blank lines into paragraphs; in each paragraph drop every line whose trimmed form starts with `|`, then collapse the rest to one line. Take the paragraphs mentioning `exemption clause`; at least one of them must also carry `never`, `re-cut` and `observable predicate`. Stripping the table lines is load-bearing: without it, row 4's cells satisfy the assertion and the ban paragraph can be gutted while the case stays green — that is exactly the hole INC-1's second review round found. Breaks: delete the ban paragraph; replace `Never patch a working rule` with `Consider avoiding patching a working rule`; delete `Re-cut the rule` from it; replace `Re-cut the rule on an observable predicate instead` with `Re-cut the rule on your best judgement instead` (criterion 6, the observable predicate).

Criterion 4 — both audiences reached, nothing restated.

9. The home exists and is scoped to both. `.claude/rules/authoring.md` is a file, and the frontmatter between its first `---` and the next one contains both `skills/**` and `agents/**`. Break: delete the file, or drop either pattern from `paths:`. (The pre-existing scoping cases at test-repo.sh:60-121 add, for free, that the page is path-scoped at all and that both patterns match tracked files.)
10. The skill-page author is pointed at it. `skills/CLAUDE.md` contains the string `.claude/rules/authoring.md`. Break: delete the pointer sentence.
11. The agent-page author is pointed at it. `.claude/rules/agents.md` contains the string `.claude/rules/authoring.md`. Break: delete the pointer sentence.
12. One home for the ban. `grep -lie 'exemption clause'` over `agents/*.md`, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `skills/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `rulebook.md`, `README.md` and `GEMINI.md` returns exactly `$root/.claude/rules/authoring.md` and nothing else; on failure the case prints the paths it found. 13. One home for the table. The same ownership check keyed on `rationalisation`, the table's most distinctive word. Break, either direction: restate a table row on another page, or delete row 1 from the owner.

## Deliberately not covered

Nothing beyond the criteria is tested: the page's opening prose, its citation of the measured source and its closing paragraph about its own placement carry no criterion, and pinning their wording would make every future reword a suite failure for nothing. ## The form of a description

A description names the occasion to reach for the thing it fronts — the
situation that calls for it, and what it hands back — and never walks through
the steps inside it. A description that summarises a workflow becomes the
shortcut agents take instead of reading the body: one measured case ran a
